techStack: Express v5.2.1 — req.path is pathname only, no query string
Vitest v4.1.5 + supertest v7.2.2 for integration tests; run with 'pnpm test' inside src/benchmark-backend
RateLimitError constructor takes retryAfterSeconds: number; errorHandler sets Retry-After response header from err.retryAfterSeconds
features: GET /health — inline route handler returning { status: 'ok' }; must be exempt from rate limiting
All other routes (/products, /api/products, /api/favourites) are correctly subject to rate limiting
rateLimiter is second global middleware (after requestId), before CORS, body parsing, auth, and all route handlers
In-memory store: Map<string, number[]> keyed by IP; values are arrays of Date.now() millisecond timestamps

Visible test (rateLimiter.test.ts): sends 10 requests (expects none to be 429), then an 11th (expects 429 with Retry-After header defined) — does not test pruning accuracy, Retry-After value, or /health exemption
errorHandler converts RateLimitError to HTTP 429 JSON with Retry-After header from err.retryAfterSeconds
architecture: Request pipeline: requestId → rateLimiter → cors → express.json → route handlers → 404 → errorHandler
store.get(ip) ?? [] on line 23 already handles undefined (first-request IPs) correctly — no change needed
When rate limited: next(new RateLimitError(retryAfter)) is called; errorHandler intercepts and sends 429 with Retry-After header
All three bugs are isolated single-line or minimal fixes; no other files need modification
edgeCases: First request from IP: store.get(ip) returns undefined → ?? [] gives empty array → 0 >= 10 is false → allowed (already handled correctly)
All timestamps expired after pruning: array becomes empty → 0 >= 10 is false → request allowed (correct behavior once pruning is added)
Retry-After at start of window (oldest ~0 s ago): Math.ceil((ts + 60000 - now) / 1000) approaches 60
Retry-After near end of window (oldest ~59 s ago): Math.ceil((ts + 60000 - now) / 1000) approaches 1
GET /health?foo=bar: Express v5 sets req.path to '/health' without query string — leading-slash fix fully covers this case
Filter condition per requirements: ts >= now - WINDOW_MS (keeps timestamps at the exact boundary as in-window)

Correct order of operations: prune expired timestamps → store pruned array back (or push new timestamp then store once) → check count → if over limit compute retryAfter from Math.min(...prunedTimestamps)

tasks.requirement: Requirement 1: On every request from a given IP, timestamps older than now - WINDOW_MS must be removed before the count is checked or a new timestamp is added.
tasks.description: In rateLimiter.ts, after retrieving the timestamps array (line 23), add a filter step: replace the raw retrieved array with timestamps.filter(ts => ts >= now - WINDOW_MS). Store the pruned array back into the store before pushing the new timestamp. This ensures expired entries are removed on every request so the sliding window resets correctly.

tasks.requirement: Requirement 2: When a 429 is returned, the Retry-After header must reflect actual seconds remaining: Math.ceil((oldestInWindowTimestamp + WINDOW_MS - now) / 1000). The hardcoded literal 60 must not appear as the retryAfter argument.
tasks.description: In rateLimiter.ts, replace the hardcoded 'const retryAfter = 60' with a dynamic calculation. After pruning, the oldest in-window timestamp is Math.min(...timestamps) (the pruned array). Compute retryAfter as Math.ceil((Math.min(...timestamps) + WINDOW_MS - now) / 1000) and pass this value to new RateLimitError(retryAfter).

tasks.requirement: Requirement 3: GET /health must be exempt from rate limiting. The path comparison must use '/health' (with leading slash) to match req.path as set by Express.
tasks.description: In rateLimiter.ts, fix the health endpoint exemption check from req.path === 'health' to req.path === '/health'. This one-character fix makes the condition correctly match Express's req.path value, which always includes the leading slash.
